excerpt: Toss is South Korea's financial super app from Viva Republica, combining money transfers, payments, Toss Bank and Toss Securities. Users, funding, IPO plans and alternatives.
content:
Toss is a South Korean financial app made by Viva Republica. It started in 2015 as a simple way to send money between people, according to Retail Banker International, and has grown into what is often called a financial super app: one app for transfers, payments, banking, stock trading, loans, insurance comparison and credit scores. The Korea Herald reported in October 2024 that Toss had 28 million members and 19 million monthly active users as of June 2024.

Several businesses sit under the group. Toss Bank is an internet-only bank, Toss Securities is a mobile brokerage, and Toss Payments handles online payments for merchants. The Korea Herald reported that Toss Securities set up a US subsidiary, Toss Securities Americas, in July 2024. Toss also offers a buy now, pay later service, launched in March 2022.

Viva Republica was founded in 2013 by Lee Seung-gun, who remains its CEO. The company has raised large sums from Korean and international investors. Retail Banker International reported a $405 million Series G in December 2022 led by Tonic Private Equity, at a valuation of $7 billion (KRW 9.1 trillion), with existing backers including Korea Development Bank, Altos Ventures, Goodwater Capital and Bond Capital.

Viva Republica has been preparing to go public. In February 2024 it picked Korean underwriters for a domestic listing, but in October 2024 it halted that process and said it was considering a US listing instead, Korea JoongAng Daily reported. The same report said it posted an operating loss of 9.4 billion won in the first half of 2024, sharply narrower than a year earlier.

The Toss app is free to download. Fees apply to some services, such as card payments for merchants, trades and loans, and are shown in the app.

This page is research, not a review. We have not used Toss; facts come from the reporting listed under Sources.

use_cases: Sending money to friends and family in Korea
Banking with Toss Bank, an internet-only bank
Trading Korean and US stocks through Toss Securities
Paying online and taking payments as a merchant through Toss Payments
Checking credit scores and comparing loans and insurance

fit: people living in South Korea who want their finances in one app
Korean retail investors trading domestic and US stocks
Korean online merchants that need payment processing
not_fit: people outside South Korea: most services need a Korean account and phone number

pricing.intro: The Toss app is free. Individual services such as trading, loans and merchant payments carry their own fees, shown in the app or on each subsidiary's site. We did not find a single official price list.

plans.name: Toss app
plans.detail: Service-specific fees shown in the app

pros: One app for transfers, banking, investing and payments
Very large user base in Korea
cons: No single public fee schedule across services
